clue.text: No-hoper in party admitting violation? Not initially

indicators.note: a thing admitting something lets it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: not initially tells us to drop the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: a wrong is a violation

explanation.surface: A useless person hangs around at a party where some offence is being committed.
explanation.walkthrough: Drongo is Australian slang; 'party' looks like part of the scene but is the outer shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Drongo is Australian slang for a stupid, hopeless person, a direct synonym of no-hoper.

clue.text: Setter, perhaps, with set of steps left out producing conflict

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter for left is taken away

parts.note: a flight of stairs
L is short for left

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, missing a flight of stairs, provokes a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' invites thoughts of the compiler, but it is the gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogfight is a close aerial battle or any fierce scrap, a kind of conflict.

clue.text: Comparatively stupid baronet stuck in one river before another

indicators.note: stuck in means lodged inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river
Bt is the abbreviation for baronet
R stands for river

explanation.surface: A rather dim aristocrat gets stuck in one river after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire (and another in Sussex); 'before another' places the second river at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow-witted, so the comparative obtuser means more stupid than another.

clue.text: Fail in game by inventor? Certainly

parts.note: Go is a Japanese board game
Alexander Graham Bell, inventor of the telephone
yup is informal for yes, certainly

explanation.surface: Asked if a game by some inventor would flop, the reply is yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To go belly up is an idiom for failing completely, especially a business going bankrupt.

clue.text: Plant is shortly an enticement to tour parks when cultivated

indicators.note: to tour something is to go all the way round it, so one piece surrounds the other
shortly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a lure is an enticement

indicators.note: cultivated ground is turned over, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener's note on a flower that draws visitors round the parks where it is grown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant is' reads as part of a sentence, but 'is' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden flower, a delphinium relative, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Muck a horde sprayed around Dutch aristocrat's area

indicators.note: around says one group of letters encloses the other
sprayed letters are scattered about and land in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
D is short for Dutch

explanation.surface: A rabble throwing filth about a Dutch nobleman's estate.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdukedom is the territory ruled by an archduke, a high-ranking noble, so his domain.

clue.text: Japanese art covered by broken doorway

indicators.note: covered by means held inside the following words, concealed within them

parts.note: spans the end of broken and the start of doorway

explanation.surface: A Japanese artwork sits hidden behind a damaged entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is Japanese sword-fighting with bamboo staves, one of the martial arts.

clue.text: Food taken by Scottish footballers with wee dram

parts.note: the Pars is the nickname of Dunfermline Athletic
a nip is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A Scottish team has a meal with a small whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Dunfermline Athletic, a Scottish football club, are known as the Pars.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a root vegetable, an everyday item of food.

clue.text: Member of Providence's electorate ignoring very unruly person in mob

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: Providence is the capital of Rhode Island, RI, and a member of an electorate is a voter
V is short for very

explanation.surface: A voter in Rhode Island, disregarding everything, turns violent in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Providence is a US city, capital of the state Rhode Island, abbreviated RI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rioter is someone taking part in a riot, a violent disturbance by a crowd.

clue.text: Secures extra, we hear, and makes do

parts.note: to get something is to secure it

indicators.note: we hear means the words are to be taken by their sound, not their spelling

parts.note: a bye is an extra in cricket, a run scored without the bat touching the ball

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a little extra and so manages to scrape along.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is one of the extras, runs not credited to a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by is an idiom for managing or coping with limited means, the same as making do.

clue.text: Projected plan in races arranged with nothing to follow

indicators.note: arranged letters are set out in a fresh order rather than the order given

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A race organiser's schedule of fixtures with a blank day after them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing to follow' puts O after the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a postulated sequence of future events, an outline of what is expected to happen.

clue.text: Like one getting abuse around amateur — and cut off from elsewhere?

indicators.note: around says one piece is placed so as to surround the other

parts.note: someone given abuse has been insulted
A is a standard abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: A sports amateur taking a barrage of insults ends up feeling cut off from everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: insulated usually means protected, here stretched to isolated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insulated is isolated or protected from outside influences, kept apart from the world around it.

clue.text: Musical detected in middle of aria?

parts.note: surface reading: something found in the central passage of an operatic song
setter's reading: the middle letters of aria are R and I, and R stands for rex, the king

explanation.surface: A musical theatre fan spots something in the middle of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: R, from Latin rex, is the crossword king, so the two central letters of aria spell out the show's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The King and I is the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical set in Siam.

clue.text: Regular features in column disheartened colleague having little weight

indicators.note: regular features are letters taken at even intervals, every other one

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart, every letter between the ends, is removed

parts.note: only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist's regular pieces mention a dejected workmate who has lost weight.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small unit of weight, about 28 grams, so it is literally a little weight.

clue.text: Manager to plunder a Liverpool player before game, reportedly

parts.note: to harry is to raid or plunder
Liverpool FC are nicknamed the Reds

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the word is matched by sound

parts.note: nap is a card game; the K is silent

explanation.surface: A football manager's order to raid a Liverpool player ahead of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Redknapp is an English football manager, formerly of Tottenham, Portsmouth and West Ham. Nap (Napoleon) is a trick-taking card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Redknapp is best known as a Premier League football manager, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Ready to admit a point in Catholic church I have condensed

parts.note: taken as written
C is an abbreviation for Catholic
CE is the Church of England
pt is short for point
I've is I have contracted

explanation.surface: A doctrinal point within the Catholic church, explained briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: The order is loose: the point follows the church abbreviations rather than sitting inside them. Acceptive is a rare word.
explanation.definitionFit: Acceptive means inclined to accept or receive, so willing to let something in.

clue.text: Fussy waiter's round back of table in a kind of way

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around another, enclosing it
fussy suggests fidgety, restless movement, so the letters are shifted about

parts.note: taken with the 's that follows it

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A fastidious waiter circles the end of a table in a particular manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s of waiter's supplies the S for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: As it were is a phrase meaning so to speak, softening a word used in a kind of way.

clue.text: Disrespect pro overturned in loyalty to organisation

indicators.note: something overturned is upset and thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A professional's insubordination is overruled for the sake of the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit de corps is the shared pride and devotion of members of a group to that group, a near paraphrase.

clue.text: Learned prince not seen in country with awful diet

indicators.note: not seen in means absent from, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: Peru is a South American country
P is short for prince

indicators.note: awful means very bad, a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clever prince stays away from a country with terrible food.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudite means scholarly, having much learning, so learned in the adjective sense.

clue.text: Banter in border of park?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: scolding or ranting talk
second meaning: a fence of rails edging a park

explanation.surface: Light-hearted chat going on at the edge of a park.
explanation.walkthrough: To rail at someone is to complain bitterly; the clue stretches this to banter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for complaining talk and a noun for a fence of bars around grounds.

clue.text: Interfere in Florida location by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is matched to how it is pronounced

parts.note: Tampa is a city in Florida

explanation.surface: Someone meddles in affairs somewhere in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the final -a and -er sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamper is to meddle or interfere with something without permission.

clue.text: Notice in the last month one no longer in minority

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a notice
ult., short for ultimo, means of last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: An announcement last month that someone has come of age.
explanation.walkthrough: Minority here is the legal state of being under age, not a smaller group.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult has reached the age of majority, so is legally no longer a minor.

clue.text: What regular sun worshipper might see in winter dance?

parts.note: a keen sunbather acquires a tan
without summer sun, the colour fades away

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what a sunbather would notice during the colder months.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as a whole: in winter the sunbather sees their tan go.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance that originated in Argentina.

clue.text: Courageous fielder in decisive part of match?

parts.note: game means plucky, willing
point is a cricket fielding position square of the batsman

explanation.surface: A brave fielder makes the crucial play in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket setting points away from tennis, where the answer belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: Game point is the stage in tennis where one more point wins the game, a decisive moment in a match.

clue.text: Moving painting recreated with love for impressionism foremost

indicators.note: recreated means made over again in a new form, so the letters are reordered
putting one thing for another means swapping it in place of the other
foremost picks out the leading letter of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, written O
its first letter

explanation.surface: An emotional painting is redone in a loving, impressionist style.
explanation.walkthrough: One I of PAINTING becomes O, giving PAONTING to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something poignant is touching and evokes sadness, the emotional sense of moving.

clue.text: Figure of speech producing amused response around island

indicators.note: around says one piece sits inside the other, enclosed by it

parts.note: a smile is how one responds when amused
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A turn of phrase that raises a grin around an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile is a figure of speech comparing two things with like or as.

clue.text: Straight men taken in by much of vivid and showy speech

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it
much of a word is most of it, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: rich colours are vivid
het is short for heterosexual, straight
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Heterosexual men are swept up in lavish, flamboyant oratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straight' wants to mean honest or direct; here it is slang for heterosexual. OR, other ranks, is the crossword's usual men.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is persuasive, often pretentious language, speech designed for display and effect.

clue.text: Group in football somewhat trouble a guest

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following words is used, sitting inside them

parts.note: spans the end of trouble, all of a and the start of guest

explanation.surface: Football club members cause a visitor some bother.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an association of clubs competing against each other, as in the Premier League.
